tasks.short: Administer anaesthesia and monitor animals under veterinary direction

steps.what: Verify the animal, veterinarian's directions and anaesthesia equipment
Administer anesthesia according to the veterinarian's directions
Monitor animals' responses and coordinate any dosage adjustment with the veterinarian

tasks.design: Retain preparation, administration and response monitoring under veterinary direction. Existing protocols in {DOCS} support the task; no dosing model or autonomous adjustment is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Animal-specific response and physical administration need trained attention.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's human-healthcare tools do not establish veterinary anaesthesia automation.
tasks.still_hard: Rapid physiological changes and individual response.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises changes and coordinates promptly with the veterinarian.
tasks.altitude: No change in clinical time or prescribing authority.

evidence.claim: Veterinary anaesthesia administration and monitoring remain trained human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician anaesthesia work, excluding veterinarian labour, postoperative recovery and separate drug-log entry.

Veterinarian supplies patient-specific directions through existing care work; technician verifies them in s1's25 hours and observes actual responses in s3's35 hours. No structured ready-for-anaesthesia or safe-dose flag is assumed.
Local authorised scope governs action. No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which actions remain technician duties alongside existing monitoring devices?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no administration or monitoring time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Care for and monitor animals recovering from surgery

steps.what: Monitor the condition of animals recovering from surgery
Provide directed recovery care and escalate unusual changes to the veterinarian

tasks.design: Retain direct recovery checks and physical care. Existing postoperative guidance in {DOCS} supports trained staff; no automatic recovery classification replaces observation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery depends on actual animal condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated veterinary recovery change is supplied by the digest.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises changes and acts within the care plan.
tasks.altitude: No change in recovery care time.

evidence.claim: Direct animal recovery observation and care remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician postoperative recovery, excluding anaesthesia monitoring in task4176 and other staff's care time.
Technician produces observed recovery signs in s1's60 hours; no structured normal-recovery flag is assumed.
No new system or upkeep is added, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which recovery changes require direct observation and veterinary review?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, zero upkeep; no recovery care effort is removed.

tasks.short: Maintain controlled drug inventory and log books

steps.what: Count controlled drug stock and verify product identity, units and physical balance
Capture and verify each controlled drug receipt, use, waste or correction transaction
Enter verified transactions and balances into the controlled drug log books
Reconcile the ledger against physical balance and investigate discrepancies

tasks.design: Test the approved controlled-drug ledger in {OTHER}, the veterinary practice system, for single transaction capture and automatic balance posting. Retain physical counts, exact transaction approval and discrepancy investigation; no unexplained balancing correction is allowed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified transaction facts may be copied into separate ledgers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native ledger rules can post checked quantities and maintain an audit trail.
tasks.still_hard: Physical quantities, wastage and unexplained differences need accountable checks.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks the physical stock and investigates discrepancies.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate ledger entry; inventory responsibility remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: A native controlled-drug ledger can reuse verified transactions; veterinary legal acceptance and savings need local validation.

assumptions: Boundary is technician stock counting and ledger maintenance, excluding drug administration, prescribing and any separate required witness time, which remains unchanged.

Technician produces product and batch identity, strength, unit, opening balance and physical count in s1's40 hours, then captures transaction type, signed evidence, quantity, time and case reference in s2's25 hours. The exact posting is approved there. Missing evidence or inconsistent units block posting and require manual investigation in retained work.
Test a locally approved native ledger first; legal record and witness requirements must be confirmed before replacing any paper process. Existing automatic entries earn no saving.
unknowns: Local controlled-drug record and witness requirements
research_questions: Can single capture remove copying while preserving approved records and physical reconciliation?

incremental.description: Maintain ledger fields and investigate posting exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact transaction snapshot including drug, batch, strength, units, quantity, type, time and evidence from s2; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional B100 R80 gives20 gross minus4 upkeep net16. Low assumes only4 hours duplicate copying removed; physical count40, capture25 and reconciliation15 remain full. Already automatic ledgers have no new labour-saving case.

steps.what: Observe animal behavior and condition and monitor clinical symptoms

tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated veterinary observation automation.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle changes may require repeated observation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices changes and refers concerns appropriately.
tasks.altitude: No change in observation time or diagnostic authority.

evidence.claim: General animal observation remains human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is general observation, excluding anaesthesia in task4176 and postoperative recovery in task4177; those hours are not added again here.
Technician produces actual symptom and behaviour observations within s1's100 hours. No structured change flag or free classification input is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which subtle signs require direct comparison with baseline behaviour?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, zero upkeep; all general observation remains, with specialised monitoring excluded from this task view.
